sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Regent University and Walden University differ notably in ownership, enrollment, tuition, and location. Regent University is a private nonprofit institution located in Virginia Beach, with an undergraduate enrollment of 4,729 students and an in-state tuition of $21,650. In contrast, Walden University is a private for-profit institution based in Minneapolis, enrolling 9,136 undergraduates and charging an in-state tuition of $12,762. These distinctions highlight differences in institutional structure, scale, cost, and geographic setting between Regent vs Walden and Regent vs Walden.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing Regent University and Walden University in terms of cost, Regent University charges an in-state and out-of-state tuition of $21,650, whereas Walden University has a lower tuition rate of $12,762 for both in-state and out-of-state students. The median debt for students who complete their programs at Regent University is $24,534, which is higher than Walden University's median debt of $20,834. These figures illustrate the financial differences between Regent vs Walden and Regent vs Walden, reflecting variations in tuition fees and student debt burdens.
